instruction: Using the command line, count the number of data rows (excluding the header) in file1.xlsx on the Desktop. Save just the number to ~/Desktop/row_count.txt.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent converted file1.xlsx and file2.ods to CSV using libreoffice --headless, merged columns with paste -d '', created output.csv. Then struggled to open LibreOffice Calc from terminal due to lock file and display issues. Ran out of turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use terminal commands (ls, head, paste, cat, wc), convert xlsx/ods to CSV via libreoffice --headless --convert-to csv, pipe and redirect output
metadata.failure_analysis: Model successfully converted files and merged data but spent too many turns trying to launch LibreOffice Calc from terminal. LibreOffice had lock file issues and the model kept trying different approaches without resolving it within turn limit.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests the model's ability to convert spreadsheet to a parseable format and use shell tools to count rows. This is a data inspection sub-task within the model's demonstrated capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires converting xlsx to CSV, then counting data rows (excluding header). Getter reads the output text file. Metric checks if the file contains '5000' (file1.xlsx has 5001 rows including header = 5000 data rows). Partial credit (0.5) for off-by-one errors.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads /home/user/Desktop/row_count.txt matching the instruction's output path
Metric correctly handles expected parameter as rules dict (expected.get('expected_count')) - proper get_rule pattern
Metric uses regex to extract numbers from file content, correctly matching '5000' for full credit
Sensible partial credit (0.5) for off-by-one errors (4999/5001) handling header inclusion ambiguity
Full instruction coverage: single requirement (count rows excluding header, save to file) is verified by checking output file content
Expected value '5000' is consistent with metadata claim of 5001 total rows including header, though not independently verifiable without the actual xlsx file
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider verifying the expected_count of 5000 against the actual file1.xlsx data to confirm accuracy
